comments.author: @gsp8489
comments.text:
1:20 The Midwest is not bound by our silly concepts of borders. It is above of all that. It spans from the Eastern third of the Dakotas, the top half of Missouri, to the Eastern edge of Indiana, to the southern halves of Michigan, Wisconsin, and Minnesota. Western 2/3rds of the Dakotas is "the plains" or just 'the west'. Southern Missouri is the south. Northern MI, WI, and MN have other cultural identification that is distinctly different from that of the PURE and undefiled midwestern states like Iowa, Indiana, Illinois and fall under  "great lakes" or "Northwoods" region. The only states whose borders lay 100% within the midwest region are Iowa, Illinois, and Indiana. This is settled. It is not up for debate. Good day. 

p.s. Ohio in not midwest. Whether or not 'the East' accepts them is not my concern. If not, They can be their own thing.
